quick_english: Then the supreme means of the great lord is praised, the supreme word indeed.
What was declared as mere light, the supreme Bhairava greatness, has only freedom distinguished there.
That light gives light-ness to all; nothing exists apart from it, and the universe appears as being.
Therefore that supreme lord, unbarred in his own self-space, reveals the spectacle of creation and destruction.
As earth, water, and so forth shine unmixed in a pure mirror, so world activities appear in one conscious lord.
Similar shining appears in eye, mirror, sky, and water; indeed, in pure form only form appears.
Though the hidden passionate woman touches with her breast-pots the mirror reflecting her beloved beautifully, she is not satisfied.
Indeed touch of it is not pure; form alone is so, because purity is extreme dense union of same kind.
Purity, as the guru taught, is the seeing capacity of the different arising from non-difference in self, for one who does not abandon self-light.
Purity is primary for the one consciousness-lord; elsewhere it is partial, by his will.
For beings, the obstructive body-maya nature belongs to them only; true-knowledge nature is non-obstructive.
Thus revealing an appearance of both forms, the boon-giver shines everywhere by image and reflection view.
Someone may argue that rays from the eyes strike a clear surface, bounce back, and thereby grasp one's own face; such a person is now questioned.

tokens.grounds: self as knower of external light
same light as instrument of knowing

quick_english: If the self, presiding over light outside the body, could know by that very light, then what need would there be for a mirror?

tokens.grounds: rays now act as knowing agents

quick_english: If the reversed rays became the graspers, the form would be seen on one's own face, not inside the mirror.

tokens.grounds: form would appear as directly present
image is purely an object of sight

quick_english: If it were really one's own face, that form would appear on one's own face, like touch, as 'mine'; but the mirror image is not tangible and has the nature of being only something seen.

tokens.grounds: other sensory qualities absent or suppressed

quick_english: The reflected image is only the shape of visible form; the real thing, joined with touch, smell, taste, and the rest, has those other qualities suppressed in the reflection.

tokens.grounds: image lacks contact and location in mirror

quick_english: Suppression is due to the absence of graspability, but that does not prove the thing is absent; and that non-graspability arises because there is no real contact with the object and because the image does not actually reside in the mirror.
For this reason, properties such as heaviness are not observed in the image; it is not actually situated in the mirror, which serves only as a means for seeing it.

Therefore, what appears does not exist there as something separate; the mirror is called its support only conventionally, while lamp, sight, and awareness are, in sequence, the real means of its appearance.
Lamp, eye, and cognition do not produce a separate mirror-like appearance, because they lack hardness and are supremely pure and clear on all sides.
The God of gods revealed this for the understanding of the deluded: a thing may appear even elsewhere than where it is, yet not fully or truly there.
The compassionate teacher explained that the image is not solid, not independent, and not simply stable or unstable; rather, it is the special power of some clear medium.

The teaching on the mirror declared that a reflection has no fixed place, no independent form, no time, no measure, no mutual contact, no removal, and no solidity; it is not simply unreal, nor does it have an essence of its own. By understanding this, delusion is dispelled.
In the account of reflection presented here, the reflection of sound is what is called an echo.

The echo is not produced by the original sound coming back, because although it is heard as if returning, the speaker does not hear it in that way and distant listeners may not hear the original sound at all.
Because an echo changes according to the hollows or openings it meets, the reflection of sound behaves like the reflection of a face or other visible form.
Just as a mirror shows the form of another object, an echo is heard as something spoken by another.
Because a reflection must face its original, the perceivers who stand between the source and the reflecting place are the ones who hear the echo.
A reflection can be perceived even without perceiving the original directly, just as one may see in a mirror the body of a beloved person standing behind oneself.
Facingness is explained as the reflection's being situated in non-difference from the mirror-like condition in which it appears.
Therefore, in the hollow space of a well or jar, the speaker's space is reflected together with sound and appears as if another speaker were there.
Just as someone standing behind a mirror does not directly know the face, someone standing behind such a reflecting space does not directly know the original sound.

tokens.grounds: two aspects of the original sound

quick_english: An unmanifest sound is not reflected; its manifestation and hearing occur at the same time, in the second moment.
In that moment, the sound's being reflected and its being heard occur at the same time, just as one does not ascertain a hand and its shadow at different times.
Now that the true nature of reflection has been shown here, we return to the main topic, for reflection properly applies there.
Sound is reflected beautifully in space, and touch too can appear as something external, like a blow, pain, or cold, yet it agitates one's own body because it is a reflection.
This reflected touch is not the primary one, because it does not reveal an independent chain of effects of its own.
In the same way, smell appears within the organ of smell, and taste appears clearly in the moisture of the mouth.
Just as a reflected form is not seen without the eyes, taste, touch, fragrance, and the rest are not perceived without their proper sense organs, even if they are present.
The object of the cognition of an external touch is not located inside the inner field of touch.

tokens.grounds: conditions for the reflection to act
reflection taken up in the organ

quick_english: When one's nearby sense organs and inner instruments are properly engaged, the reflection received in the sense organ produces a corresponding activity.

An action does not arise from a remembered mental object, because such action truly belongs to the present. Therefore, the excellent touch is situated in that sense organ, having arrived there and being known, and it acts accordingly in the present.
When an external object is impossible, that same excellent touch, reflected within one's own self, produces that pleasurable sensation. It does so within some continuum of subtle channels.
Therefore, by offering the universe as his own self in the mirror of consciousness, this declares the pure universal nature of the Lord.

tokens.grounds: objects of sense appearing in reflection
taking on the quality of the reflecting surface

quick_english: Just as smell, form, touch, taste, and other qualities, when reflected, shine in a sword by taking on the coloring of that support, like a face and other images reflected there.

tokens.grounds: state and dependence of the universe
qualities constituting the nature of consciousness

quick_english: Likewise, this universe, reflected in consciousness, should be understood to rest upon its expansive qualities, such as luminosity and freedom.
Just as a reflection from all sides may appear in a crystal that is clear on all sides, so too reflections appear in consciousness, which possesses complete clarity.
Absolute transparency is the non-manifestation of one's own form. Therefore consciousness is the most transparent, unlike a jewel, which grasps and displays its own form.
A reflection is projected by an external original image, but if everything is a reflection of consciousness itself, what external original image could possibly remain?
Even if some cause is designated as an external original image, it too becomes a reflection in consciousness; otherwise, outside of consciousness, it would be unreal.
Thus, protected by the firm weapon of the logic of one's own awareness, the sovereignty of reflection alone expands everywhere.
An objector asks how a reflection can exist without an original image. The reply is: what can we do, for it is seen? The objector is then challenged to identify that supposed original image.
It is not so, because the supposed original lacks the required definition. What is truly called an original image is something unmixed with others, independent, and truly appearing, just like a face.
They define the nature of a reflection as resembling another form without abandoning its own nature, like reflections seen on a sword, a mirror, or a flat surface.
And it is said by the Buddhists that even if external objects exist, cognition is one because it perceives many; it takes on forms resembling many, but it does not itself become many.

But what, then, is the definition of a reflection? It is stated as the impossible manifestation of difference from its substrate due to the unfitness for mixing with another, just as a face appears in a mirror.

This universe, beginning with the supreme reality, is mixed with consciousness and cannot be manifested as different from consciousness; why, then, should it not be called a reflection in consciousness?
If this arrangement of the definition is arbitrary, then let the universe be called the original image. Wise people are concerned with reality itself, not with conventional terminology.
But surely a reflection cannot exist without an original image? What of that? In a reflection, the original image does not exist as a separate entity, for it exists only in identity with it.
So, even if this stated definition is impossible, there is no loss in taking it as a mere cause; rather, the question comes to rest there.
Even in the case of what is called an instrumental cause, and not a material one, instrumental causes cannot in any way be possible at any time or place.
For this very reason, when light is present before one, the form of the beloved may appear vividly transferred there through memory and similar instrumental triggers.
Otherwise, why would the beloved, who is actually separated, appear as present in consciousness? Consciousness does not go out in front to reach that separation.
Therefore, let there be some inner factor called intellect, in which appearances arise clearly by division, as in imagination and in the seeing of dreams.
Therefore, let the Lord's powers be the instrumental cause in such cases. Thus this whole universe is a pure reflection in the clear sky of Bhairava-consciousness, not by the grace of anything else.
That power of the Lord, independent of anything else, by which he is the self of the universe, is declared to be the supreme, unsurpassed goddess Pratibhā.

tokens.quick_gloss: shining in the spreading of Kula

quick_english: Of this Lord Akula, the supreme power is Kaulikī, who shines in the spreading forth of Kula; the Lord is never separated from her.

tokens.quick_gloss: that which is the pure union of those two

quick_english: The pure united form of those two is remembered as saṃghaṭṭa. That same union is called the power of bliss, because from it the universe is emitted.
This goddess is declared to be the principle beyond the supreme and the non-supreme. She is its essence and its heart; that supreme emission is the Lord.
In the Devīyāmala scripture she is described as Kālakarṣiṇī, and likewise in the Mahāḍāmaraka rite the glorious supreme goddess is placed at the head.

tokens.quick_gloss: as the true nature of the mothers
that reflective awareness of being consciousness in this union

quick_english: In the Śrīpūrva scripture she is described as the true nature of the mothers, as that reflective awareness of being consciousness within this union.
The supreme will-power of the fierce powers is the lord; that same power, when agitated in form, becomes the ruler.
Then fierce supreme goddesses are born as guides of the shaiva path; self-reflection, formerly the single hero, arises.
Established by knowledge-power, this supreme-lower goddess, whose self unfolds the knowable universe, creates the fierce circle of mothers.
It continuously creates the lamp of pure and impure paths; when the knowable portion comes with rising agitation from strength.
Deficiency-appearance arises in pure consciousness; then the established knowable class is called the beginning of stability.
This establishment is the grasp of varied forms in the ocean of awareness; yogis collect this seed of seed-arrangement.
Will-power, said to be two-formed and agitated or unagitated, indeed rests in the self through the duality of objects.
By the quickly shining power of fire-form, desired attainment occurs through stability in the earth-self.
Although this is knowable in the unfolding power abundantly, nevertheless that is the place of glory, not the eastern birth-place.
Thus from will-power they say four-formed supreme nectar; because there is no inner agitation, this is not the seed of anyone.
Agitating-nature, seed-nature, support of agitation, and womb-nature are named; the form of consciousness is agitated and also agitates.
Agitation would be the knowable quality; agitating is its exclusion, while the inner undivided one-seed desire to emit remains.
Agitation in that will is the appearance of truth-will; they know agitating, and having attained unity, that will becomes effective.
The sons of Shri Somananda call this support of agitation the undifferentiated distinctness of the beginnings of consciousness.
Whatever is only knowable is that seed; by union, seedness is in sound; that same seed's desire to emit is the origin from which this grasped shining different form of consciousness-self arises.
This is agitation; agitating, however, expels the silent other-mother-going and the sudden indifference-part from consciousness by force.
Although born, that desire to emit becomes accomplished from the unity of other reflection; thus the support of agitation is proclaimed.
Then that knowable interval desires a different form from the universe-seed; all external reflection will manifest.
The true nature of the agitated-agitating state has been shown by me, as spoken by Shri Maheshvara, by the grace of the guru.
We speak of the subject; this is not seed, the four letters, nor does it attain the status of support of agitation.
In the self only, by rest, that spoken immortal nature; thus the previously spoken fivefold is mutual.
From the mutual mixing of rising varied forms, the supreme higher vibration and bliss rise together.
From that collision of will-unfolding going to great variety, supreme bliss-consciousness is in will-power when employed.
Thus the triangle is called beautiful emission-bliss; supreme bliss-powers attain establishment there.

tokens.quick_gloss: by the joining of two triangles
to the state of six spokes
even in the joining of unfolding

quick_english: When two triangles join, the configuration moves into a six-spoked state; yet even in that unfolding, it goes again into absorption in that same reality.

tokens.quick_gloss: arisen in the unfolding of will
is said also of that movement

quick_english: The stirring that arises in the unfolding of will, mutually interacting, clearly manifests the form of the power of action; this is also said of that movement.
Those two powers indeed share that same form and do not stand otherwise. But how can unsurpassedness and bliss, which by their own nature are free from division, appear in this way?

tokens.quick_gloss: Lord of consciousness whose nature is unlimited

quick_english: How can those two, free from division, take on such variegation within their own self? Listen: this Lord of consciousness is by nature unlimited.

tokens.quick_gloss: lord of phases of dissolution and arising of endless power-variety

quick_english: If the great Lord, master of the dissolution and arising of endless varieties of power, were to remain in only one form, then what would follow?

tokens.quick_gloss: that would abandon like a pot and such

quick_english: He would abandon his great-lordship and his nature as consciousness, like a pot or any other finite thing. For limited luminosity is indeed the defining mark of the inert.

tokens.quick_gloss: surging in the great ocean of awareness

quick_english: Awareness is distinct from the inert because it cannot be measured. Therefore, his own powers surge up like waves in the great ocean of awareness.

tokens.quick_gloss: the variegation of their own self-union
the diversity of their own self-union

quick_english: Like waves, they take on the variegation of their own self-union. That mutual diversity of the powers is the diversity of their own inner union.

tokens.quick_gloss: where the three powers have become clear

quick_english: They declare this very diversity to be the supreme, clear body of the power of action, in that fourteenth abode where the three powers have become manifest.
Therefore the Teacher declared this to be the trident in the Śrīpūrva teaching, and teachers who see reality have also called it stainless.
The power-holder seems affected because will, knowledge, and action appear separately; yet power itself is never affected by anything.

tokens.quick_gloss: by its own desired and other modes

quick_english: That same triad, through the power-holder's own modes such as willing and the rest, appears clearly; but when it shines forth in unity, then it does so as one.

tokens.grounds: the triad of powers is not to be grasped by any limiting condition
reason why no single aspect can be exclusively adopted
the three powers of will, knowledge, and action
metaphor for the unified triad of powers
result of entering the trident of powers
state of the yogi freed from limitation

quick_english: Because the three powers cannot be grasped by any one-sided condition and mutually resist such limitation, they become a single vibrant trident. The yogi who quickly becomes absorbed in that trident becomes stainless.

tokens.grounds: an eightfold sequence starting from the supreme nectar level
the octad expands into sixty-four through the forms beginning with Brahmi

quick_english: In this way, the octad that begins from the supreme nectar state, when divided through Brahmi and the other forms, clearly expands into eight octads.

tokens.grounds: the highest power is the subject in this phase
the form appears in a manifest state
concession: manifestation occurs without loss of essence
manifestation takes the form of bindu due to the knowable aspect

quick_english: Here the supreme power, even while making her own body manifest, takes the form of bindu because of the stain associated with the knowable aspect.

tokens.grounds: temporal condition of the power of action
the locus where the supreme bindu is recognized
the triadic field of soma, surya, and agni
absence of division in that light
the luminous nature identified as bindu
the supreme point or seed of manifestation

quick_english: When the power of action has arisen in the abode of moon, sun, and fire, the undivided light that is present there is, for us, the supreme bindu.

tokens.grounds: scriptural source cited for the doctrine
location of the bindu in yogic experience
the bindu contains the threefold nature

quick_english: And in the teaching on the protection of the principles, the supreme Lord said that the bindu stands within the circle of the heart-lotus and has a nature consisting of the human, power, and Shiva.

tokens.grounds: instruction to the practitioner or reader
the bindu is understood through modes of absorption
qualities of the bindu in this state
introduces the sound identified with bindu
the bindu is experienced as resonant sound
the audible or subtle sonic form

quick_english: The bindu should be understood, through the distinction of dissolution, as pure and delivering. It is that sound whose nature is nada and which is present in all beings.

tokens.grounds: describes the apparent directional structure of nada
examples of experiential variations attributed to light

quick_english: Though described by divisions of below and above, it remains without activity. Whatever variety appears, such as soothing or sharp qualities and white or red colors, belongs to that apparent diversity.

tokens.grounds: the light is independent in its own nature
light does not depend on those variations
ordinary source of light denied as ultimate illuminator
fire also does not ultimately illuminate

quick_english: That light is in itself independent of those variations, as the teacher said. Neither the sun, nor the moon, nor even fire illuminates it.

tokens.grounds: their dependence on the higher light
the luminosity they appear to have
consciousness is the true source of appearance

quick_english: Sun, moon, and fire have no splendor of their own apart from that light. Rather, it is consciousness that shines in this way.

tokens.grounds: explains how one light appears diverse
the differentiated qualities it seems to take on

quick_english: Joined with varied conditions that arise from its own freedom, the one light takes on an inner variety, such as sharpness and other qualities.

tokens.grounds: the sun is normally too intense for direct viewing
sunlight reflected or falling on water
the medium that conditions the light
the same light becomes pleasant through a condition
directs attention to the power of the limiting medium
the condition shapes the experience of light

quick_english: Even the sun, which is hard to look at, becomes delightful to the eyes when its light falls on water. See how powerful a conditioning medium can be.

tokens.grounds: the same light appears limited in external objects
conditioned light depends on supreme consciousness

quick_english: The light seen in the sun and other things is stained by limiting conditions, and therefore it depends on the Maheshvara light, the light of consciousness itself.

tokens.grounds: technical name for the illuminating aspect
the aspect that brings forth the knowable content
technical name for the object-manifesting aspect

quick_english: Clearly manifest mere light is called the sun. That aspect which pours forth the essential content of what is to be illuminated is called the moon.

tokens.grounds: epistemic role of the sun aspect
epistemic role of the moon aspect

quick_english: They call the sun the means of knowing and the moon the object to be known. Though never separated from each other, the two also stand as independent.

tokens.grounds: the dyad becomes a mutual orientation of subject and object
the state reached by the pair
the name for the unifying agni aspect

quick_english: When this pair, as enjoyer and enjoyed, turns toward each other, there arises a blazing form of consciousness that is proclaimed as fire.

tokens.grounds: identifies the supreme principle of fire
identifies fire's supreme principle with the knower
refers back to the supreme principle
the knower's principle is pure consciousness
consciousness does not depend on an external knowable

quick_english: The supreme principle of fire is nothing other than the knower's own reality. It is consciousness itself, not dependent on anything else because it is identical with what is to be known.

tokens.grounds: the knower is defined by autonomy
the knower appears in diverse forms
the fire aspect grows through the diversity of knowable objects

quick_english: Because of its freedom, consciousness is called the knower. It appears varied through differences among knowables, expanded by the diverse appearances of objects that arise on the moon side and are taken up by the fire aspect.

tokens.grounds: draws the consequence of the previous explanation
authoritative naming of the fire aspect
consciousness does not rely on external epistemic means
the subject whose status is being described

quick_english: For this reason the great Lord called this fire Citrabhanu. The status of consciousness is entirely independent of the whole set of means that begin with the knowable.

tokens.grounds: describes the self-established status of consciousness
analogy for derived or reflective knowing
such a knower lacks immediate self-evidence
derived knowing depends on experienced objects

quick_english: Consciousness stands as the immediate sense, 'I am the knower.' But one who knows like a person who merely knows scripture is not truly knowing in essence, because that knowledge depends on experienced objects rather than on its own self-form.

tokens.grounds: defines the condition of derived knowership
the term is used only by fitness
the designation is secondary or provisional

quick_english: That is not true knowership which depends on a pure knowable or anything similar. In such a state, the term knowership is used only in a secondary sense, because of a certain fitness.

tokens.grounds: it is a conceptual construction of limited subjectivity
its manifestation is not divided by time

quick_english: That dependent knowing is only a kind of measuring, constructed by the limited knower. Consciousness, even when it surges forth, is not divided by temporal sequence.

tokens.grounds: consciousness is complete at the moment of manifestation
contains the whole cognitive triad within itself

quick_english: As soon as consciousness arises, it is already full and contains within itself the knower, the known, and the rest. Ordinary actions like cooking, by contrast, unfold in sequence because they are limited by time.

tokens.grounds: addresses a possible objection about sequential action
the completed nature of the action

quick_english: Even if one thinks of an action as ending in a final moment, that alone does not make it the completed act of cooking. In this way, the principle of light is established as having the nature of moon, sun, and fire.

tokens.grounds: the underlying unity of the triad
the triadic division does not remove unity
introduces the first form in the triad
identifies the first form as sun

quick_english: Even so, the primary nature of these three is not removed: they remain mere light. Of these, the first, short form is called the sun.

tokens.grounds: instrumental cause of the name Soma

quick_english: Because of long rest arising from stirring and bliss, it is called Soma. That supreme state, named Pluta, is established beyond the bliss of Soma.
Those skilled in scripture call that light-natured state fiery. Here, when the three abodes are established, what remains is mere light.

The seventeenth kala, therefore having the form of nectar, spreads forth through the movement of the bindu of its own higher and lower nature.

But at the terminal point of visarga it is called supreme Kundalini, and also the space of Shiva; it is called the supreme abode of the self of Brahman.
Mere visarga is the Lord's play of creation and dissolution: it is the casting of his own self into his own self, the state belonging to visarga.
Visarga, thus emitted and having reached a contracted state, is defined as Hamsa, as breath, as a consonant, and as a stop consonant.
That unsurpassed supreme abode is called Akula. The visarga of that Lord is called the Kauliki power.
That very same state of visarga, when bliss rises in sequence, becomes a surging forth that extends to clearly manifest action-power.
Visarga indeed, having drawn in so much otherness within itself, is like the ocean in this form: an endless succession of waves.
Therefore this visarga, consisting of the unmanifest ha and ka, is called the principle of Kama in the revered Kula cave.
That imperishable unmanifest, situated in the throat of the beloved, is of the nature of sound, without desire, and free from meditation and concentration.
Having fixed the mind there, one should subdue the world all at once. Therefore, just as visarga abides clearly in Hamsa, so too is its state understood.
In the same way, those beginning with Anuttara abide as the range from ka to sa. From Anuttara comes the clear emanation of the fivefold ka-group.
Because it is necessarily of the nature of the five powers, this is clear in each case, as the power of will, abiding in its own nature, appears from a single form.

From that twofold power are born the pair of groups beginning with ṭa and ta. But from unfolding comes the pa-group, because through it the universe is completed.
This, having the form of the knowable and extending up to the twenty-fifth, is clearly manifest. Because it is knowable and thus clear, this much is declared to have the form of the stop consonants.
And the power of will, which is twofold as stirred and unstirred, turns toward a portion of a different power and goes to the state of ya.
That very same power, more quickly tinged by the stain of the knowable, and turned toward what is different, goes to the state of ra and to the state of la.
In the same way, the twofold unfolding power, when it moves toward the power of otherness, becomes the letter va, which pours forth the essence of creation.
Will itself, having reached supreme bliss, is called air when joined with swiftness; through shining it becomes fire, and through firmness it becomes earth.
This group of four is said to be inner because it is contained within will and the other powers and abides in its own completion.
The joining of the same-kind powers, beginning with will, is said to be a form of agitation, and this also applies to those whose nature involves both agitation and nonagitation.
When the supreme meets its own sameness, a twofold movement arises. One of these remains simply the supreme and can give rise to bliss.
In that joining, a clearly agitated union arises. Even here the supreme abode is present, and the second aspect also serves the purpose of bringing something forth.
Without agitation, the supreme nature is not sufficient. Will may lack action, or it may be tinged by what is to be willed.
Divided by swiftness and firmness, will becomes threefold, appearing as unopened, opening, and fully opened.
What is willed appears threefold within will without losing its essential form, brought forth by will's own inner heat, which is the impulse of its freedom.
When the triad of śa, ṣa, and sa is clearly projected outward, it stands forth; and from that, in the letter sa, the whole universe shines clearly.

tokens.quick_gloss: in cessations of beginning-and-end of agitation

quick_english: Yogins declare that this is the immortal, supreme abode. In the cessations at the beginning and end of agitation, that very state is known as the supreme nectar.

tokens.quick_gloss: in absorptions of hissing-sound bliss and true-being

quick_english: In absorptions marked by the hissing sound, bliss, and the sense of true being, that very state is declared to be the supreme, undivided absolute.
The Blessed Lord himself taught this in the glorious Kula mystery, a text whose true name arises from the unity of power and the holder of power.
Out of affection, he revealed to you the poison-principle called anacka, shaped like a crow's beak-cavity and beyond meditation and concentration.
The true principle of desire is revealed as fullness in union, and the true principle of poison is revealed as nectar when concealment falls away.

For the will-power present there is the one that has been declared, and that very will-power produces its own task inwardly, in the form of what it desires.
What stands there as the cause of tinging is the object to be willed. From that aspect there is no true production; what arises from it is turbidity and its form.

tokens.grounds: divine correlates of the six vowels

quick_english: Those six deities are the principal rays of the sun, and within those very solar rays there is a lunar digit.
Therefore the triad of long vowels is clearly a lunar body; and the moon is nothing other than the enjoyable and the enjoyer—there is no third thing apart from them.
The enjoyer alone becomes established as twofold by appearing as the enjoyable; for a pot does not have enjoyability as its own nature—rather, that belongs to the subject.

tokens.grounds: mode by which the unsurpassed appears

quick_english: Therefore, the establishment that occurs in the subject is called the object's enjoyability; the unsurpassed appears through the states of being the object of awareness and the subject of awareness.

tokens.grounds: dynamic union of subject and object modes

quick_english: The enjoyable—will and the rest—attains the form of a collision; likewise, when will and the other powers rest on the ground of unsurpassed bliss, they become enjoyable.
The arising of the juncture phonemes is said to be the form of the enjoyer, and the god who is made of unsurpassed bliss is said to be the enjoyer alone.
Will and the rest are only the enjoyable, and for that reason they are his powers; if the enjoyable dissolves into the enjoyer, then the enjoyer becomes clearly manifest in his true reality.
Therefore the triad, essence of six, of consciousness-will-opening nature, that same threefold, they call Bhairava's supreme greatness.
That triad of the supreme lord is the full power sung; by it the universe is drawn, because in this worshipped.
Worship born in a cut and barren universe-power: thus this greatness is only so much, and that much is not possible.
Who would make a limit to the power of the unlimited? Therefore the god is supreme by freedom and supremacy.
Endowed with emanation power, completed as universe-formed; thus the great lord has fifty-reflection full power.
Reflection-self is one; indeed other powers are established in this only; the eighty-one-footed goddess will be included here.
In one reflection nature, sound-mass is Bhairava; by reflection-shadow and union, that same power is mother-power.
She is different in womb from sound-mass collision; Malini is as before ninefold reflection, having separate class nature.
In each reflection ascent, that same is fifty-natured; thus by sound penetration, supreme reflection is natured.
Shiva, as mother and father, maker, is established everywhere; emanation indeed is power; this again is as Shiva-bindu.
Womb-made infinite universe, he resorts to supreme selfhood in unlimited universe inner essence, in own self of the lord.
Supreme reflection is indeed called, marked by duality attainment, in supreme emanation self, Shiva-Shakti nonduality.
Supreme reflection is called I by fullness of the lord; supreme first emanation ending is power-natured.
In withdrawn all-universe supreme, she dissolves; that universe stands within power, she supreme in supreme.
That her thus, what is true, by the lord enclosure-making; by that, in Trishika treatise, power's enclosed form.
In consciousness shines which universe; there also indeed by consciousness; that triad has gone to compaction by pair union.
One only supreme form of Bhairava is I-self-natured; emanation power of Shambhu thus exists everywhere.
From that indeed all this bliss essence agitation; for thus in sweet song, touch, or sandalwood etc.
In mediacy disappearance, which throbbing in heart is bliss power; that same called, because heartful person.
First, having abandoned all duty in void fire, mind-rest named, then after that.
Toward seen, heard, etc. things in own consciousness, mind awakening called, Shakti-joy fullness natured.
There towardness, that thing collision of thing; in heart, of rising; by fullness entry, limited mind dissolution in Shiva.
As before future towardness possible limited dissolution from, mind dissolution named this, emanation Shambhava supreme.
In essence protection rite thus, emanation triad is said; in heart lotus sheath middle, those two collision is desired.

quick_english: That which is red is fire; its vigor is sun-and-moon-bodied; thus the letter 'a' is supreme Brahman, whose nature is the arising of that collision.

tokens.grounds: in the form of food as object of enjoyment
consisting of sound, touch, and taste

quick_english: That seed too has a supreme vital power made of the five elements. As something to be enjoyed it takes the form of food, consisting of sound, touch, and taste.

tokens.grounds: because it causes increase of vital power
whose nature is the desire to emit

quick_english: Sound too is sweet because it increases vital power. That vital power is supreme and pure, and it is understood to have the nature of a desire to emit.

tokens.grounds: from that vital power come offspring and

quick_english: That vital power is strength, vigor, the vital breaths, and loveliness. From it offspring arise, and it is also spoken of in ritual acts.

tokens.grounds: the state of having all forms

quick_english: In sacrifice and other rites, in rain, in plants, again in vital power, and then in offspring, the same power circulates. Thus emission takes on the form of the whole universe.

tokens.grounds: from entering the state of being agitated and agitating, Malini

quick_english: That whole mass of sound is called Matrika. Because it enters a state of being both stirred and stirring, it is also declared to be Malini.

tokens.grounds: beautiful through the union of seed and womb and the arising of emission
is determined to be the power
having the form of the universe

quick_english: Malini, beautiful through the union of seed and womb and the rise of emission, is indeed determined to be the supreme power that takes the form of the whole universe.

tokens.grounds: through connection with the differentiation of the power-holder
the state of being a pair

quick_english: In reality this supreme power is one alone and draws forth time. Yet through its connection with the differentiation of the power-holder, it takes on the form of a pair.

tokens.grounds: whose nature is the perfect I
because of freedom would manifest division

quick_english: That reflective awareness, whose nature is the perfect I, abides in its own self and, by its freedom, manifests division within itself.
When division appears, this awareness is said to take a threefold body: Pashyanti, Madhyama, and the gross level called Vaikhari.

tokens.grounds: according to gross, subtle, and supreme
beautiful with a flow of tones

quick_english: Each of those three also has a threefold form: gross, subtle, and supreme. Among them is a form beautiful with flowing tones, having the nature of sound.

tokens.grounds: because letters and so on are not yet divided
the state of being a single undivided form

quick_english: That gross aspect is indeed Pashyanti. Since letters and other divisions have not yet appeared there, its single undivided form is called sweetness and power.

tokens.grounds: arising from friction of articulatory place, breath, and so on
from functioning in proximity to consciousness

quick_english: Clearness and harshness arise from the friction of articulatory place, breath, and so on. Yet in this sound-form they function in close proximity to consciousness.

tokens.grounds: immersion in body and so on

quick_english: Absorption into that same sound is perceived suddenly. Those who do not become absorbed in it remain sunk in the body and similar limitations.

tokens.grounds: but with the measure of consciousness sunk and not centered in the heart
whatever comes from a skin-covered drum and so on

quick_english: Those who do not know remain with their awareness sunk and not centered in the heart. For them, the sound that comes from a skin-covered drum or the like is just an external resonance.

tokens.grounds: because of being clear and unclear, Madhyama
and of Madhyama the presence of an undivided aspect

quick_english: Because it is both clear and unclear, that gross form is Madhyama. Madhyama also contains an undivided aspect, which is described as its coloration.
Where sound is made of undivided tones, it is delighting. Non-division brings fulfillment, as can be seen in the recitation of rhythm.
One feels satisfied in that unmanifest sound during musical playing. Yet that same level can also serve as the cause for the arising of clear letters.

tokens.grounds: that connecting awareness like the first

quick_english: That gross level is Vaikhari, whose function is mainly sentences and other articulated speech. Even within this gross triad there is a connecting awareness like the first.
When that triad is taken separately, it is called subtle. It is seen in experiences like 'I make the note shadja,' 'I play sweetly,' and 'I speak words.'

tokens.grounds: which form is without limiting condition

quick_english: A threefold connecting awareness is indeed experienced separately. Of that triad, the first aspect is a form without limiting condition.
That is the supreme triad. There Shiva is of the nature of supreme consciousness, and in the manifestation of division three principal powers appear.

tokens.grounds: the power of unfolding called knowledge

quick_english: The three principal powers are Anuttara as supreme will, the power situated as supreme-and-non-supreme, and the unfolding power called knowledge, which is declared as the lower.

tokens.grounds: again from their stirring form are declared
from immersion arisen as the power of action

quick_english: From the stirring of those powers, six immaculate cognitions are declared. They arise from the immersion of those same powers as the power of action.

tokens.grounds: this much of the God of gods

quick_english: Twelve cognitions are declared, and in them all is contained. This is the principal wheel of powers of the God of gods.

tokens.quick_gloss: by being of the nature of reflective awareness
through union with emission and projection
tokens.grounds: by the joining of outpouring and casting forth

quick_english: To this extent, the God of gods, Bhairava, possessed of full power, is of the nature of reflective awareness and is united with emission and projection.

tokens.grounds: because of cognition that determines a fixed extent

quick_english: Because of knowledge that measures limitation, these powers are called Kalikas in some places; and in the revered Sara scripture, the supreme one-syllabled power is said to be in the middle.

tokens.quick_gloss: one should worship the one called Bhairava-self
tokens.grounds: worship her named as the self of Bhairava
encircled by a group of twelve yoginis

quick_english: One should worship the power called the Bhairava-self, surrounded by twelve yoginis; from them the circle of powers extends up to sixty-four.

tokens.quick_gloss: in many ways in the scripture

quick_english: Beginning from the syllable e, it unfolds up to the thousand-spoked; and in the scripture these powers are given many names according to their different functions.

tokens.quick_gloss: through forms of duality, nonduality, and mixture
tokens.grounds: by the joining of dual, nondual, and mixed modes

quick_english: Their modes of worship, in dual, nondual, and mixed forms, have been explained at great length in the revered Traishira.

tokens.quick_gloss: from fear of prolixity and from lack of usefulness
tokens.grounds: because of fear of expansion and because it is not useful here

quick_english: It is not written here, for fear of prolixity and because it is not needed; those same powers are proclaimed as stainless, pure, and not-terrible.

tokens.quick_gloss: of the terrible and more terrible
and because of being the source
tokens.grounds: and because they give rise to them

tokens.quick_gloss: in the transcendence of those three limiting conditions
tokens.grounds: beyond the triad of those conditions

quick_english: Because they are the source of the terrible and more terrible forms, they are also of that nature, appearing in creation, maintenance, dissolution, and in the transcendence of those three conditions.
The abiding form of those same powers is divided in many ways, but the teachers say that the form beyond limiting conditions is twofold.

tokens.quick_gloss: from the non-arising of limiting conditions
by the method of forceful ripening
tokens.grounds: through the process of intense maturation

quick_english: This may be because limiting conditions do not arise, or because they are calmed; and that calming is twofold, either by quieting or by the method of forceful ripening.

tokens.quick_gloss: by what is called the savor of devouring
tokens.grounds: through the relish known as assimilation

quick_english: The pacification called forceful ripening, fully active through the continual blazing savor of devouring, is the one fit for instruction, because it burns up the fuel of difference.

tokens.quick_gloss: in the fire in the belly of one's own awareness
tokens.grounds: in the digestive fire of innate knowing

quick_english: When all things are forcefully offered into the fire of one's own awareness, they kindle that fire by their own power and abandon the division of difference.

tokens.quick_gloss: they consume what has become nectar
tokens.grounds: they eat the world transformed into immortality

quick_english: When, by forceful ripening, the divided forms of things are dissolved, the goddesses of consciousness consume the whole universe as it becomes nectar.

tokens.quick_gloss: resting solely in the full heart
tokens.grounds: lying exclusively in the plenary heart

tokens.quick_gloss: Bhairava of the sky of consciousness
tokens.grounds: Bhairava who is the space of awareness

tokens.quick_gloss: they repose upon the god without difference
tokens.grounds: they rest in nonseparation upon that deity

quick_english: Satisfied, they repose without difference upon the god Bhairava, the sky of consciousness, who rests solely in the full heart of their own self.

tokens.quick_gloss: from entry into acts and functions and from the multiplicity of names and worships
tokens.grounds: because of immersion in activities and because names and worships are many

tokens.quick_gloss: the form appears even in non-difference
tokens.grounds: the form shines forth even though there is no difference

quick_english: Thus, because of their entry into various acts and functions and because of the many names and forms of worship, their manifold form appears even within non-difference.

tokens.quick_gloss: of the goddesses through the joining of invocation and dismissal
tokens.grounds: of the goddesses by the practice of bringing in and sending out

tokens.quick_gloss: by one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, and nine and more
tokens.grounds: through increasing numbers beginning with one and going beyond nine

quick_english: And of these very goddesses, through the joining of invocation and dismissal, there is an expansion by groups of one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, and more.

tokens.quick_gloss: the extensive division beginning with Rudra, Arka, Anya, Kala, Sena, and so on
tokens.grounds: the broad differentiation starting from Rudra, Arka, Anya, Kala, Sena, etc.

tokens.quick_gloss: now to the matter at hand

quick_english: The extensive division beginning with Rudra, Arka, Anya, Kala, Sena, and so on is vast; enough of further detail—now the discussion turns to the matter at hand.

tokens.grounds: in the manner of a reflected image

quick_english: This whole expanded group of things shines in the self of consciousness as a reflection; one for whom it appears thus is indeed the Lord of the universe.

tokens.quick_gloss: for whom such a non-conceptual awareness
tokens.grounds: who has this kind of thought-free recognition
sealed by the method of Shambhu

quick_english: One in whom such a non-conceptual reflective awareness is ever arising in the self is indeed marked by the Shambhava means.

tokens.quick_gloss: the reflective awareness of full I-ness
mantra, mudra, ritual action, and worship other than that
tokens.grounds: other practices such as mantra, gesture, rite, and worship

quick_english: This is the reflective awareness of full I-ness that has been explained; here there are no other practices such as mantra, mudra, ritual action, or worship.

tokens.grounds: known by the further name of living liberation

quick_english: Resorting again and again to this non-conceptual immersion, one attains the state of Bhairava, also called liberation while living.

tokens.quick_gloss: even by a brief indication there is this framing of means and goal
tokens.grounds: even in summary form the distinction of method and object is set out

quick_english: From this point onward, liberation while living is examined, where even in brief outline the distinction between means and goal is set forth.

tokens.grounds: thus in the path without means

quick_english: But in the previous chapter there was not even a notion of difference; therefore, in that means-less path, who is liberated, how, or from what?
In the non-conceptual reflective awareness called the Shambhava means, the wise person should apply the fiftyfold division that was indicated earlier.

tokens.grounds: even the element earth, in a thought-free way
beholding, reaches the state of Bhairava

tokens.quick_gloss: this same method applies also to water and the rest
tokens.grounds: this procedure holds for water and so on as well

quick_english: Seeing even the earth itself, without conceptualization, as reflected in one's own self, one attains Bhairava-hood; the same method applies to water and the other elements as well.
At the final limit, one conceives a supreme principle beyond all coverings, all-pervading, independent, all-knowing, and called Shiva.
Seeing even that conceived Shiva reflected in the mirror of unconstructed, noble awareness, and free from conceptual thought, one becomes Bhairava oneself.
Just as one who sees a red object in front with nonconceptual awareness becomes firmly established in the undivided awareness of that one pot through its various channels.

tokens.grounds: extends the analogy to all aggregates

quick_english: In the same way, recognizing one's own self through each and every aggregate beginning with earth, one shines forth as truly full.
This has arisen from me, this is reflected in me alone, and this is not different from me: in this threefold way is the Shambhava means.

tokens.grounds: states that the summary is given

quick_english: This is the summary of creation, maintenance, and withdrawal. As it is established and taught, the Spanda teaching states it.
By this alone the supreme sovereign nature of awareness and its identity as the self of all are made known; what other defining mark need be stated?
In my own self, in the space of consciousness, I manifest the universe; through this expansive recognition as the creator whose self is the universe, Bhairava identity unfolds.
The entire group of the six paths is reflected in me alone; recognizing 'I am the maker of maintenance' is this clear universal form.
Seeing that this universe melts in me, in the self matted with the flames of ever-risen great awakening, one becomes still.
I am Shiva, the exulting fire that burns the dream-house of samsara, filled with endless varied beings.

The whole world arises from me in many differentiated forms, yet when it dissolves in me no other remains. One who sees creation, maintenance, and dissolution as play in a partless reality shines forth in the fourth state.
In that supreme means, abounding in Shaiva non-duality, some indeed attain trust, being cultivated by the lord of bound souls.
Bathing, vow, body purification, retention, mantra application, path arrangement, sacrifice rite, offering, recitation, and concentration.
Such imaginings are not fitted here by difference; the grace-causing state of one present here is clearly established.
If one worthy of such grace approaches the teacher, then he is such; he would not be through devotion to becoming, but cultivated.
He worships him; then, from the cultivated grace-giver, he should learn the various initiation rites.
Future ones too have those devotions; they attain completion, and this essence-state, supreme and to be obtained, is described as Shiva.
Thus this supreme Shaiva self-knowledge has been told in great detail.
